66551dfd88.q: How did Altoids grow from a regional Seattle brand to become the number one mint in America?
66551dfd88.a: Altoids started in the UK under Callard and Bowser, acquired by Kraft Foods, and initially only gained traction in Seattle during the 1990s. When Jeff Grace joined Leo Burnett, they unlocked what was working in the Pacific Northwest and helped stoke those flames across America. Within about five years, Altoids had bested Certs and Tic Tac to become the number one mint in the country, all while spending only $10 to $15 million a year in ad spend compared to competitors spending $50 to $60 million annually.
66551dfd88.rq: Her goal is like to eliminate plastic from the fashion industry. This was Jeff Grace, a veteran in the advertising industry who together with his wife, Stacey, founded the underwear brand Kent.

406f5b6e48.q: What is Kent's core mission and why did the brand shift from premium silks to sustainable basics underwear?
406f5b6e48.a: Kent was originally a high-end silks brand founded by Stacey with a sustainable, plastic-free mission, but it had become a premium $400 camisole brand that excluded most customers. When Jeff and Stacey re-examined the brand's first principles, Stacey realized her original goal was to be the most radically natural brand on earth. They pivoted to a basics apparel business focused on underwear because it's the one product customers cannot donate to thrift stores—it only has one lifecycle. They made compostability their primary proof point and claim that every piece of Kent clothing, including packaging, is fully biodegradable and compostable.

809992a869.q: Why did Kent avoid paid advertising for over five years despite Jeff's advertising background?
809992a869.a: Despite being an advertising veteran, Jeff and Stacey observed that many D2C brands in the VC-funded era were operating as leaky buckets—spending $800 million annually to generate only $750 million in revenue. They watched brands like Allbirds and Bonobos struggle after aggressive paid advertising spending. Instead, Kent focused on optimizing their website conversion and reducing product lines that weren't working, squeezing more efficiency out of organic traffic. They are only now considering paid advertising after nearly reaching $1 million in revenue and exhausting website optimization opportunities.

c50eca94e4.q: What was the inspiration behind Kent's brand name and its connection to Superman?
c50eca94e4.a: Stacey chose the name Kent because it is clean, simple, and has a nice resonance when spoken. The deeper connection is to Clark Kent, the Superman character who removes his clothes to reveal his superpower—making it a fitting underwear metaphor. The name has become so optimized for search that Kent appears in Google results before the county of Kent in England.

e584d6fcf8.q: What marketing channels does Kent prioritize for a D2C underwear brand?
e584d6fcf8.a: Jeff prioritizes email marketing as the primary channel, spending considerable effort to create the best emails possible. Social channels come next, followed by PR which has been very effective for Kent. Influencer partnerships rank fourth—Jeff views each influencer as their own agency with built-in media plans (their audience), deep connection with followers, and content creation included. Only after optimizing these channels does Kent consider paid advertising on platforms like Meta.
